features.title: Cross-Session background jobs board
features.summary: The Jobs tab of Observe › Processes: One page lists every background job of every Session: running jobs projected live from the job registry, finished or interrupted ones from the session logs, classified into deterministic categories derived from the job kind and label.
reach: expect text "What runs on this host for your threads*"
failureModes: A job of another Session is listed and described, but stopping it goes through the registry's owner fence, not a client-side bypass.
A job whose output ring belongs to an earlier DSH process reports that only its lifecycle record was retained instead of an empty output.
A malformed session-log record is skipped without dropping the rest of the file or the persisted index.
A missing or malformed index state file is rebuilt by rescanning the logs instead of failing the board.
An unreadable sessions root leaves the board listing live jobs rather than erroring.
The retained history is bounded, so old jobs age out predictably.

externalDependencies.boundary: Read-only projection of the live job registry plus the human kill; the board never starts or mutates a job record.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: src/service.test.ts drives a registry stub that delivers registry events and records the fenced read/kill calls.

externalDependencies.boundary: Imports the published `session-log` frame reader to resume session logs at a byte offset; the board reads no usage state.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: src/history.test.ts writes plain JSONL session logs and asserts the incremental resume and the merged lifecycle rows.

verification.testName: clamps an unbounded live view to the wire bounds so the board still parses
reads the package manager script that did the work, not the wrapper around it
names the producer kind for jobs that are not shell commands
lists running jobs before finished ones and pages with a cursor
counts and filters by the category derived from the command
marks a recorded job without a settlement as interrupted until a live twin overrides it
reads a live job output as its owner and refuses output from an earlier process
kills a running job as its owner and reports a settled one as already finished
records job lifecycle events, session titles and a settled/unsettled status
resumes from the persisted offset and reads only the appended records
rebuilds from the logs when the state file is malformed

telemetry.testName: records a background-jobs history pass span with the files it read

features.title: Stop a selection of running jobs
features.summary: Running rows carry a checkbox; Shift/Cmd select ranges and toggles, select-all covers the visible running rows, and stopping the selection goes through one confirmation that names the count. Each kill still passes the registry's owner fence.
features.currentSurface: left-nav: Background Jobs: Jobs › batch stop
failureModes: Finished rows have no checkbox, so a batch can never target a job that already settled.
A kill the owner fence refuses stays selected and is reported instead of being retried without the fence.

verification.testName: reports requested, already-finished and failed kills separately

telemetry.reason: Client-only: Stop a selection of running jobs renders browser state and starts no Host work of its own.

features.title: Observe › Processes: jobs, dev servers and RAM on one page
features.summary: One Processes page (plans/ade-ux §6 "Processes in 3 boards") owned by background-jobs: Jobs, then the tabs other plugins add through the `@dshfiles/background-jobs/process-views` registry (Dev servers from preview, RAM from worktree-memory). Its navigation glyph carries their marks (RAM pressure and detached memory). `ProcessesNavigation` lets the former RAM page and saved tabs land on their tab; palette rows find it by the old names (Background Jobs: Jobs, Worktree Memory: RAM).
failureModes: A provider cannot replace the Jobs tab; one tab per id, the first registration wins.
Without providers the page is the Jobs board alone, with no tab row.

verification.testName: orders tabs after Jobs, one per id, and never lets a provider replace Jobs

telemetry.reason: Client-only: the page composes tabs; its reads are the jobs-board, dev-server and RAM features' API calls.

features.title: Thread panel Jobs facet
features.summary: A Jobs tab in the thread panel (the right pane's tab chooser): this thread's background jobs with output and Stop, then each Processes view that can filter to one thread (its dev servers, the RAM its process trees use), and a link to Observe › Processes. Registered as a right-pane page tab type, so it follows the thread on stage without changing sidebar-right.
failureModes: Stopping a job goes through the registry's owner fence, as on the board.

verification.testName: gives the Jobs facet only the views that can filter to one thread
